reviews.comment: Took Dr. Kim for my required "Becoming-a-History-Major" type of Directed Study class for transfer students. He teaches you how to cite, borrow a book from the library, etc. I'm sure he's a great professor in a real class; I can tell. He talks about his work a lot but he's cool. Take him for a real class!!!
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kim is super great at writing and really cares that you do well. I took 404 with him as well and it was great. Listen to lectures, pay attention to his notes about your writing, and he is always willing to provide sources for you if you need help.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor threatened multiple students with expulsion throughout the year for any quote without a source. He viewed every small infraction as plagiarism. He was a very tough grader and expected 15-page essays with all good sources. I had to request transcripts from museums in japan and have books scanned in from the library for him.

Dr. Kim has been great for 481, he just expects a lot of participation. He wants us to learn more than just how to write but how to appreciate history, so he'll expect you to be passionate, too. He's given us a lot of sources and he'll do his own research for your topic to help where he can.

Tough tests, but gives a TON of extra credit. Don't miss a class and you get bonus points just for showing up! As long as you take the class seriously, it is an easy A/B. Professor is very nice and entertaining.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kim is a super down-to-earth professor, and is really passionate about his content. Attendance is worth a good part of the grade, and he gives out a lot of bonus points. Basically all of the material comes from lectures, but he's a great lecturer, so if you pay attention you'll be fine. Very informative on what will be on each exam.

I highly recommend the class:  I do not recommend the professor.  He is arrogant, extremely slow to respond to emails (if he responds at all) and while this class was a history class, he turned it into a political science class.  He expected us to write ivy league essays in the length of a class with no preparation and his grading was ridiculous.

My fall semester of my freshman year I switched into HIST 104 last second and I could not be happier with my decision. You cannot miss this class or you will get behind because Professor Kim does move very quickly through the slides giving detailed information on every slide. This class made me appreciate history which I never had in the past.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Kim is such an amazing professor. The beginning of his class is more homework heavy, but it benefits you in the long run. He is very understanding of any problems you may have. Even though the paper is a huge obstacle, his grading process and writing workshops alleviated my stress. As long as you put in effort you will not only pass, but learn.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have ever had. Highly recommend his class. You will have to put in effort to make an A. He has a great sense of humour and always made me feel like I could be successful. #highkeylovehim

History professors can be very pompous when visiting. I can whole heartedly say that Dr. Kim is the best professor I have had at A&M. He still managed to give consistent feedback in a timely manner despite the COVID-19 transition. His class is challenging, but worth it.

This class sucked. I mean the whole semester was literally writting one paper. Was that the bad part, no, but what sucked is that every time you make progress on the paper he'd shut you down. There were plenty of times where I went from an 11 page paper to about 4 pages because what I wrote "wasn't good enough". Get as much help as you can or fail

Not an easy A, but stay consistent and youll do well. If you follow his instructions and listen to his feedback you will finish the class knowing how to write a research paper much better than prior to the class. Learned a lot in his class and the only reason I didnt make an A was because I didnt do too well on my outline and first draft.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Getting an A in HIST 280 was hard but doable. We submitted a proposal & bibliography, a 1500 word draft, the full 3000 word draft, a revised draft, & a final draft  each about 3 weeks apart. We got feedback after each submission. Dr Kim was great about giving clear, purposeful feedback and leading thought-provoking class discussions respectfully.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Kim is a great professor. His tests are essays and short answers (when I took his Japanese History class 2 or 3 years ago) but if you listen in class and do the readings you should be able to retain a lot of what you need to know. I made flash cards to study though just to make sure and I made an A. His class was interesting. I would take again

Dr. Kim manages class discussion masterfully. He manages to include himself in the discussion without being dominating and without ending discussion with his own opinions. He draws quality work from you and makes you a better historian. An absolutely wonderful professor.
Had him History 280, as it was required for my major, but he is fair. He grades fair, but tough at times, and he is very well-educated.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS
